valid_fixes: Restore SQSToDynamoDBFunction.Environment.Variables.DYNAMODB_TABLE_NAME to !Ref InventoryUpdatesTable so the consumer writes to the deployed table
invalid_patches: Create a DynamoDB table named after the stack's inventory-archive suffix to match the wrong env var — adds a spurious table instead of correcting the reference
Grant dynamodb:PutItem on '*' to the role — does not fix the non-existent table name referenced by the env var
optimal_diagnostic_path: ace_check_queue_depth(queue=InventoryUpdatesQueue) → messages present and consumer being invoked (in-flight count non-zero)
ace_get_log_tail(function=SQSToDynamoDBFunction) → ResourceNotFoundException for table ace-bench-stack-inventory-archive on every invocation
ace_get_stack_outputs() → InventoryUpdatesTableName=ace-bench-stack-inventory-updates — confirms env var references a non-existent table
ace_check_queue_depth(queue=InventoryUpdatesDlq) → DLQ depth 0 despite repeated consumer failures — messages silently dropped after maxReceiveCount exhausted
observable_symptom: The consumer function is invoked and logs show repeated ResourceNotFoundException errors referencing a table named inventory-archive that does not exist. No records are written to the database. After retries are exhausted, the messages disappear from both the main queue and the dead-letter queue — they vanish silently rather than accumulating in the dead-letter queue.
root_cause: SQSToDynamoDBFunction.Environment.Variables.DYNAMODB_TABLE_NAME is set to !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-inventory-archive' instead of !Ref InventoryUpdatesTable. The consumer calls put_item on a non-existent table, raising ResourceNotFoundException on every invocation. After 5 failed receives (maxReceiveCount), SQS attempts to route messages to the DLQ, but the execution role lacks sqs:SendMessage permission for the DLQ ARN, so DLQ delivery also fails silently and messages are dropped entirely.
